BILL NUMBER:  S5589

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the general obligations law, in relation to powers of
attorney for financial estate planning; and directing the law revision
commission to study the implementation of such powers of attorney


 PURPOSE OF BILL :
To provide technical amendments to revise Ch. 644 '08 in regard to the
execution of powers of attorney and ensure that language is used in a
consistent way throughout the statute.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
The process of revoking a power of attorney is clarified in
subdivision 3 of §5-1511. Furthermore, paragraph (e) of subdivision 1
is revised so subsequently drafted powers of attorney do not
automatically revoke previously drafted powers of attorney. In
addition, the ability of agents to act separately or jointly is also
clarified in paragraph (e) of this section.

The definition of a power of attorney is refined in subdivision 10 of

§5-1501 of the general obligations law, and the language regarding
"statutory major gifts rider" is now used consistently throughout the
statute. The gift making capacity of a power of attorney without a
statutory major gifts rider is further clarified in this section as a
maximum of $500 each year.

 JUSTIFICATION :
Ch. 644 '08 provides a comprehensive revision to the power of attorney
laws in New York State. To ensure a smooth transition, the enactment
date of Ch. 644 '08 was extended from March 1, 2009 to September 1,
2009 by Ch. 4 '09.

The technical changes and clarifications made by this bill are
necessary in order to facilitate the transition of the comprehensive
changes to the power of attorney laws made by Ch. 644 '08.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
New bill, 2009.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately.

summary: Makes technical corrections to provisions establishing powers of attorney for financial estate planning; directs the law revision commission to study, over a period of 2 years, the implementation of such provisions.
